about: One continuous push from Earth to a single synapse in one human brain, every rung a real measurement or a real photograph.
every_step_zooms_in: Checked, not assumed: every rung is strictly smaller than the one above it. The cortical surface and the tractography were dropped from this page because at 17.0 and 17.8 cm they are LARGER than the 15.1 cm brain they come out of, so the zoom had to stop and sit still in the middle. They have their own pages.
why_separate_scenes: Earth is 1.3e7 m and a synaptic cleft is 2e-8 m. Float32 carries about seven significant digits, so one scene holding both would lose the synapse to rounding. Each stage is drawn in its own units with its true field of view carried in metres beside it.

stages.name: Earth
stages.note: 12,742 kilometres across. The lights on the night side are measured, not drawn: VIIRS records the light cities throw away upward.
stages.source: Blue Marble and city lights: NASA Earth Observatory / NASA Worldview (GIBS). Satellite frames: NASA GIBS, MODIS on Terra. Aerial: USGS National Agriculture Imagery Program, 1 m.

stages.name: Eastern North America
stages.note: Eastern North America. Cloud cover is real weather on a real day, not a clean plate.

stages.name: New England
stages.note: New England, and the hook of Cape Cod.

stages.name: Boston
stages.note: Boston: the harbour, the Charles, the grid of the Back Bay.

stages.name: One block of it
stages.note: One metre per pixel. Individual buildings, individual trees, individual cars.

stages.name: A person
stages.note: One metre seventy two. The skin comes away, then the skeleton, and what is left is where the scanner found the brain, not where anyone put it.
stages.source: BodyParts3D, The Database Center for Life Science (DBCLS). Mitsuhashi N, et al. BodyParts3D: 3D structure database for anatomical concepts. Nucleic Acids Res 37, D782 (2009).

figLeaf.why: Amy wants a clothed figure; the atlas ships an anatomical one. Until a dressed model arrives, a winking emoji sits here. Measured off the atlas rather than eyeballed, so it cannot drift off the thing it is covering.

stages.name: A whole human brain
stages.note: About a kilogram and a half, and the only organ that has to be explained to itself. 283 named structures from the Allen reference atlas.
stages.source: Borner K, et al. Human Reference Atlas. Nature Methods (2025). Geometry derives from the Allen Human Reference Atlas 3D, Ding et al.
stages.limits: This is an atlas, an idealised average brain, not a person's. It is also a surface model: the structures are boundaries, not tissue.

stages.name: Into the cortex
stages.note: The folded sheet in cross section, with the white matter branching underneath it like a tree.
stages.source: Amunts K, Lepage C, Borgeat L, et al. BigBrain: An Ultrahigh-Resolution 3D Human Brain Model. Science 340, 1472 (2013).

stages.name: The ribbon
stages.note: About three millimetres from the surface down to the white matter, and that three millimetres is where almost all of the thinking happens.
stages.source: Amunts K, Lepage C, Borgeat L, et al. BigBrain: An Ultrahigh-Resolution 3D Human Brain Model. Science 340, 1472 (2013).

stages.name: Cells
stages.note: 21 micrometres per pixel. A cell body is about one pixel, so the stipple is cells: enough to see how densely they are packed, not enough to trace a single one.
stages.source: Amunts K, Lepage C, Borgeat L, et al. BigBrain: An Ultrahigh-Resolution 3D Human Brain Model. Science 340, 1472 (2013).

stages.name: One cubic millimetre
stages.note: 49,379 cell bodies, every one of them where the microscope found it. This much tissue took 1.4 petabytes to photograph.

stages.name: One neuron
stages.note: A layer 5 pyramidal cell, 3,117 synapses arriving on it, checked by hand.

stages.name: A branch of it
stages.note: One dendrite leaving the cell body, with its side branches.

stages.name: A length of dendrite
stages.note: Eighty micrometres of cable. Somewhere on this stretch is the junction the next rung shows.

stages.name: Where the synapse is
stages.note: Twenty micrometres. The swellings on the surface are where other cells arrive; this cell carries 3,117 of them.

stages.name: One synapse
stages.note: An axon ending, and the dendrite it is talking to. The gap between them is about 20 nanometres wide.
